NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday urged India's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to seize the opportunities created by the country's free trade agreements (FTAs) and take Indian products to markets across the world.Addressing the nation on the occasion of India's 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India's growing global stature and the FTAs signed with around 40 countries since 2014 had opened major opportunities for domestic businesses, particularly MSMEs."We have to reach the world. Everything that India produces should reach the world market," PM Modi said, highlighting textiles, machinery, pharmaceuticals and seafood as sectors with considerable potential to expand their global footprint.The Prime Minister, however, stressed that Indian businesses would need to meet international standards and focus on quality if they were to compete successfully in global markets.Pointing to the scale of India's ambitions, PM Modi called for a greater number of Indian companies to emerge as global leaders. He asked why India should not have 50 companies in the Fortune 500 within the next decade and said the country should aim to have an Indian bank among the world's top five.He also set out ambitions for Indian pharmaceutical companies to feature among the world's top five, while calling for globally leading Indian firms in sectors such as law, ratings, consulting and accounting.PM Modi said the country's textile industry, stretching from Ludhiana in Punjab to Tirupur in Tamil Nadu, had the potential to significantly expand its global presence. He also pointed to India's fisheries and seafood sector as another area that could benefit from the export opportunities created by FTAs.The Prime Minister said India had the talent, capabilities, linguistic strength and a long history needed to compete on the global stage. He urged businesses to build brands that could earn international recognition and turn India's economic rise into a stronger global corporate presence."India's technology companies should be a scoreboard in the world," he said, stressing that the creation of globally recognised Indian brands should be treated as a national goal.The PM also highlighted India's stable political mandate, vibrant democracy, strong judicial system and constitutional framework, saying these factors had contributed to the country's growing recognition and respect around the world.
Article Summary: Pm sets global goals on i-day. Pm modi said india's growing global stature and the ftas signed with around 40 countries since 2014 had opened major opportunities for domestic businesses. He called for a greater number of indian companies to emerge as global leaders.

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday called on people tostrengthen India's independence by making the country happy, prosperous, and secure so that the country becomes "Vishwaguru", noting that many people and forces are working against this goal.“We must make the nation happy, prosperous and secure, and ensure that it makes its rightful contribution to the world. However, many people and forces are working against this goal and creating obstacles. Without abandoning our principles, we must face these challenges and work to make India a ‘Vishwaguru’ — a guide to the world,” Bhagwat said at a gathering after hoisting the national flag at the RSS headquarters in Nagpur.Bhagwat emphasised that Independence Day is a matter of pride for all Indians. The Sangh chief stated that if the freedom struggle is traced to 1857, India’s ancestors made sacrifices for nearly 90 years to secure independence.“We feel proud of their (freedom fighters') sacrifices and are happy that their struggle reached a successful conclusion. But along with this, we must also remember that preserving the freedom achieved through so much effort and sacrifice is our responsibility,” he stressed.Saffron, he noted, represents action, knowledge and sacrifice. “The freedom of a nation is achieved through hard work and sacrifice, and after independence, these qualities help make the nation prosperous and secure.”White represents purity and discipline, while green symbolises prosperity. When sacrifice, commitment, hard work and knowledge become part of people’s lives, society remains peaceful and minds become pure, he added.Bhagwat also emphasised that individuals may hold different views, but this diversity reflects unity. “The Ashoka Chakra has many spokes, but all of them emerge from a single central point.”The Ashoka Chakra represents individual and social awareness, with its spokes kept within the limits of dharma, or discipline. “That is why we have placed this Dharma Chakra at the centre of our national flag,” he added, urging people to reflect on the flag’s symbols and incorporate their values into their lives.India will remain an independent nation, Bhagwat asserted, but its responsibility extends further: “This is our duty today” to make the country a meaningful contributor to humanity.
Article Summary: Rss chief mohan bhagwat calls on people tostrengthen india's independence by making the country happy, prosperous, and secure. “we must face these challenges and work to make india a ‘vishwaguru’ — a guide to the world,” he said.
